processing: Little is published about the method; as with Chinese black teas generally, the leaf is withered, rolled, oxidised and dried.
harvest_season: Spring is the main picking season in Zayü's tea gardens; other details are not well documented.
appearance_dry: Typical of Chinese black teas of its kind: dark, twisted strips.
taste_profile: Few tasting accounts exist, so its character is an open question; a smooth, sweet cup is what its class would suggest.

brewing.notes: A general starting point for Chinese black tea; adjust by taste.

vintage_note: A young, small-volume regional tea, normally sold from the current year's harvest as is usual for Chinese black tea. Ask for the harvest year and drink it within a year or two.
description:
Chayu black tea comes from Zayü County in Nyingchi, in the southeast of Tibet. That alone makes it a curiosity: most people do not think of Tibet as a place that grows its own tea.

The county makes white, black and green teas. Local accounts credit the plateau's climate and soil. Specifics of how the black tea is processed are scarce, so assume ordinary black tea work unless the seller says otherwise.

Detailed tasting notes are hard to come by. Brew it as you would another whole-leaf Chinese black tea, with short steeps in a small pot, and take your own notes.

Supply is small: the county reported about 30,000 jin of finished tea of all kinds from the 2025 spring season. Expect a local specialty rather than a commodity, and ask who made it and when.
history:
A person at Chayu Farm dates tea here to the 1960s, when the farm's predecessor, a land-reclamation regiment, succeeded in trial plantings. The farm presents this as the start of tea growing in Tibet, but the Yigong tea farm, also in Nyingchi, has a rival account of its own from 1963.

The county now has about 21,000 mu of tea gardens. In 2024 Chayu black, white and green teas were entered on the national list of famous, special and new farm products kept by the agriculture ministry, and received an ecological origin protection mark.
